extracted.intended_audience: instructional designers, online educators, e-learning researchers and course developers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for designing effective online learning materials and environments, including interaction design, learner preparation, activity design, and connectivist considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning should be an active process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping learners active doing meaningful activities results in high-level processing, facilitates creation of personalized meaning. Asking learners to apply information in practical situations is an active process and facilitates personal interpretation and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner knowledge construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners should construct their own knowledge, rather than accepting that given by the instructor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge construction is facilitated by interactive online instruction where students take initiative, interact with peers and instructors, and control the learning agenda. Online learners experience information first-hand, allowing contextualization and personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative and cooperative learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative and cooperative learning should be encouraged to facilitate constructivist learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working with others gives real-life group experience, allows use of metacognitive skills and peers' strengths. When assigning group work, membership should be based on expertise level and learning style so members benefit from one another's strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner control and guided discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners should be given control of the learning process with a form of guided discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learners should be allowed to make decisions about learning goals with some guidance from the instructor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection time and opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners should be given time and the opportunity to reflect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedded questions throughout lessons can encourage reflection; learners can generate learning journals to process and internalize information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning should be made meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials should include examples that relate to learners so they can make sense of information. Assignments and projects should allow learners to choose meaningful activities to apply and personalize information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactivity to promote higher-level learning and social presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning should be interactive to promote higher-level learning and social presence and to help develop personal meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interaction among content, other learners, and instructors helps learners test and confirm ideas and apply learning. Design should consider transactional relationships between instructor, learners, and content to create presence and community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Levels of interaction taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Design should incorporate multiple interaction levels: learner-interface, learner-content, learner-support, learner-learner, learner-instructor, learner-expert, learner-context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different kinds of interaction promote learning at different levels; interactions should progress from lower-level (interface) to higher-level (instructional, collaborative) based on learning theory traditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner-interface interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Interface must allow the learner to access and sense the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interface is where learners use their senses to register information. It should not overload learners and should make it as easy as possible to sense information, enabling transfer into short-term memory for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner-content interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners must interact with content to process and transform information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learners should be able to choose their sequence or be given suggested sequences. Content can be reusable learning objects or custom-created. Encourage application, assessment, analysis, synthesis, evaluation, and reflection to promote higher-level processing and transfer to long-term memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner-support interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide strategies for learner support interactions: learner-to-learner, learner-to-instructor, instructor-to-learner, learner-to-expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support strategies should also promote learner-context interaction so learners can apply what they learn in real life and construct personal meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner-context interaction and transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities should be provided for learners to transfer what they learned to real-life applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learner-context interaction allows learners to develop personal knowledge and construct meaning; transfer opportunities enable creativity beyond presented material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivist: exploration of current information
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of the information explosion, learners should be allowed to explore and research current information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learners need to be autonomous and independent so they can acquire current information to build a valid and accurate knowledge base; appropriate Internet use is an ideal learning strategy in a networked world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivist: ability to unlearn and relearn
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners must be able to unlearn old information and mental models and learn current information and models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some information and procedures become obsolete; instruction should support unlearning and learning as fields change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivist: discernment of important information
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners must be able to identify important information from unimportant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With rapidly increasing information from many sources, learners should develop skills to recognize credible, genuine, and relevant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivist: recognize outdated knowledge and stay current
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners must recognize what knowledge is no longer valid and acquire new knowledge for a discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learners need to keep up-to-date and be active participants in learning networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivist: global networking and diversity of opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners must be allowed to connect with others around the world to examine opinions and share thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Globalization and telecommunications enable experts and learners worldwide to share and review information; mobile learning supports learning anytime, anywhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivist: assemble multi-source, multi-channel information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information for learning should be assembled from many sources and delivered in a multi-channel system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not take information from a single source; use different communication technologies to reflect networked diversity and facilitate optimal learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivist: design for intelligent agents and device-specific learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that intelligent agents and built-in device learning will affect what and how learners learn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should account for embedded learning materials within devices and adapt to the equipment learners use and their prior knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivist: ongoing acquisition and experiential/authentic learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction must give learners opportunities to research and locate new information and be designed for experiential and authentic learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because learners must acquire new knowledge on an ongoing basis, online strategies should facilitate research, authenticity, and experience-based learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivist: multidisciplinary exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners must be exposed to different fields to see connections between information across disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning is becoming more multidisciplinary; curricula should expose learners to relevant fields (e.g., psychology and information technology) to understand theoretical and practical connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online instruction requires sequenced activities and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing information on the Web or linking to digital resources does not constitute online instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online instruction occurs when learners go through a sequence of instruction, complete learning activities, and achieve learning outcomes and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner preparation: rationale and pre-learning activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide pre-learning activities and a rationale to prepare learners and connect/motivate them for the lesson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rationale should show the importance and benefits of the lesson. Pre-learning activities activate cognitive structures and give the big picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner preparation: concept maps and advance organizers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concept maps and advance organizers to establish existing cognitive structures and provide the lesson's big picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concept maps incorporate lesson details and activate prior knowledge; advance organizers establish structure and bridge between what learners know and need to know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform learning outcomes and prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Learners should be informed of learning outcomes and prerequisite requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stating outcomes helps learners gauge expectations and recognize when they've achieved goals; prerequisites let learners check readiness and activate required cognitive structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide self-assessment at lesson start
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a self-assessment to let learners check prior knowledge and skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If learners already have the knowledge/skills, allow them to take the final test. Self-assessment helps organize materials and highlight important content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of learner activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a variety of learning activities to help students achieve outcomes and cater to individual needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities can include reading, listening, viewing, Internet research, learning journals, application exercises, practice with feedback, and summary generation to promote higher-level processing and closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice with feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Include practice activities with feedback so learners can monitor performance and adjust learning methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback supports self-regulation and improvement during the learning process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for reuse and small coherent segments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use learning objects and design materials in small coherent segments for flexibility and reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small segments can be redesigned for different learners and contexts; learning objects should be grounded in instructional design theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment-centred, knowledge-centred, community-centred, learner-/learning-centred design
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective learning environments are framed within four overlapping lenses: community-centred, knowledge-centred, learner-centred (learning-centred), and assessment-centred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design should attend to community and social aspects, build deep knowledge structures, respect learners' prior knowledge and cultural attributes, and integrate assessment aligned with learning goals.
